newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Micron busy as stock rallies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Micron busy as stock rallies.

text.p: A rally in shares of Micron Technology Inc touched off heavy call buying on both the Pacific Stock Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange, traders said on Tuesday.
By 1050 CDT (1550 GMT), Micron shares were up 2-1/4 at 30-3/8, just off their 30-3/4 session peak. Cumulative volume topped eight million shares.

Traders pegged the surge to an upgraded opinion of Texas Instruments Inc by Montgomery Securities, positive comments from Morgan Stanley about DRAM pricing and Micron's better than expected earnings released last week.

"There's still buying off the pre-announcement by Intel," one trader on the Pacific Stock Exchange said, referring to Intel's September 16 announcement that its third quarter revenues would be better than previously forecast.
"As Intel goes, so goes the industry," the trader said.
He said the bulk of the options activity on Micron was call buyers playing the rally in the stock.
Since September 6, Micron shares have risen from about 20.
Last week, the company reported fourth quarter earnings that beat analysts' expectations.
"We've had extreme buyers of the Oct (October) 27-1/2 calls as well as the Oct 30s," a trader at the CBOE said.
The Micron October 27-1/2 call traded more than 3,000 contracts. Its open interest was roughly 9,000.
The most active Micron call was the October 30, which traded about 7,900 contracts. Its open interest was 23,360. It was up 1-1/16 to 2-1/4 on both exchanges.
Other busy calls included the October 25s, the October 32-1/2s and the October 35s.
The October 25 was the most active put, with nearly 5,500 contracts changing hands. Its open interest was 15,930.
The October 27-1/2 put traded nearly 3,000 contracts, making it second most active. Its open interest was 4,300.
Traders said most of the activity was in relatively small blocks, generally of less than 1,000 contracts.
"It's primarily buyers but there are mixed buyers and sellers," the trader at the CBOE said.
He added that interest was mainly from institutional investors "but there's a lot of scattered retail business as well."
The heaviest activity was seen in the October puts and calls but traders said investors were also taking positions in the November and January series.
